Administrations of the Covenant
ad-min-is-TRAY-shunz
noun phrase (covenant theology)
The Reformed-confessional doctrine that the one covenant of grace was administered differently under the Old Testament (by promises, prophecies, sacrifices, circumcision, the paschal lamb, and other types and ordinances) and under the New Testament (by the preaching of the Word and the sacraments of baptism and the Lord's Supper). Westminster Confession VII.5-6.

📖 Biblical Definition

The Reformed-confessional doctrine that the one covenant of grace, substantively the same in every age, was administered differently under the Old Testament and the New Testament. Westminster Confession VII.5-6 articulates the doctrine: under the law (the OT), the covenant of grace was administered by promises, prophecies, sacrifices, circumcision, the paschal lamb, and other types and ordinances delivered to the people of the Jews, all foresignifying Christ to come; which were, for that time, sufficient and efficacious, through the operation of the Spirit, to instruct and build up the elect in faith in the promised Messiah (VII.5); under the gospel (the NT), when Christ, the substance, was exhibited, the ordinances in which this covenant is dispensed are the preaching of the Word, and the administration of the sacraments of baptism and the Lord's Supper: which, though fewer in number, and administered with more simplicity, and less outward glory, yet, in them, it is held forth in more fulness, evidence, and spiritual efficacy, to all nations, both Jews and Gentiles (VII.6). The substantive point is the unity of the covenant of grace across the two administrations: there are not therefore two covenants of grace, differing in substance, but one and the same, under various dispensations (VII.6). The OT and NT are not two different covenants of grace but two administrations of the one covenant of grace, the OT looking forward to Christ through types and shadows, the NT proclaiming the accomplished Christ through Word and sacrament. The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive doctrine against both the dispensational fragmentation (which makes the OT and NT substantively different arrangements) and the flat-equation error (which ignores the genuine progression from type to fulfillment).

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Reformed-confessional doctrine that the one covenant of grace was administered differently under the OT (promises, sacrifices, circumcision, types) and the NT (Word and sacraments); Westminster VII.5-6; not two covenants but one under various dispensations.

ADMINISTRATIONS OF THE COVENANT, n. phr. (covenant theology) The one covenant of grace administered differently under the OT and NT. Westminster VII.5-6: under the law, administered by promises, prophecies, sacrifices, circumcision, the paschal lamb, and other types and ordinances... all foresignifying Christ to come; under the gospel, when Christ the substance was exhibited, administered by the preaching of the Word, and the administration of the sacraments of baptism and the Lord's Supper... held forth in more fulness, evidence, and spiritual efficacy. The substantive point: there are not therefore two covenants of grace, differing in substance, but one and the same, under various dispensations. OT looks forward through types; NT proclaims accomplished Christ. Held against dispensational fragmentation and flat-equation error.

📖 Key Scripture

Hebrews 10:1 — "For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect."

Colossians 2:16-17 — "Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ."

Galatians 3:23-25 — "But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed. Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster."

Hebrews 8:6 — "But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The doctrine of the administrations of the covenant is held against dispensational fragmentation (two substantively different arrangements) and the flat-equation error (ignoring the progression from type to fulfillment).

expand to see more

The doctrine of the administrations of the covenant holds the substantive middle ground between two errors. The dispensational fragmentation makes the OT and NT substantively different arrangements (the OT a dispensation of law for earthly Israel, the NT a dispensation of grace for the heavenly church), obscuring the substantive unity of the covenant of grace across the testaments. The flat-equation error ignores the genuine progression from the OT administration (types, shadows, promises foresignifying Christ to come) to the NT administration (the accomplished Christ proclaimed through Word and sacrament). The Reformed-confessional doctrine holds both the unity (one covenant of grace, substantively the same) and the progression (administered by types and shadows under the OT, by Word and sacrament under the NT, with the NT holding the same covenant forth in more fulness, evidence, and spiritual efficacy). The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive doctrine: the OT saints were saved by faith in the promised Messiah through the OT administration; the NT saints are saved by faith in the accomplished Christ through the NT administration; it is one covenant of grace, one people of God, administered in two ways across the progress of redemptive history.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Westminster VII.5-6; one covenant of grace administered differently under OT (types, shadows) and NT (Word, sacraments); held against dispensational fragmentation and flat-equation error.
